policy: Selected normative technical definitions. Markdown emphasis and code markers are removed; examples and supporting observations are omitted where they are not part of the definition.

rules.C-08: Session, surface and receipt identity. Readers headers contain canonical conversation_id, native_session_id, raw source_surface, native started_at and structural discovery provenance; missing optional values remain unknown. Plugin imports carry the same optional native/surface identifiers. Map source_surface to sessions.surface and use conversation_id as the session key in all ingest paths. Source observations remain separate from immutable plugin receipt facts. Each receipt has receipt_id, canonical session/surface and received_at; child coverage rows identify only actually submitted valid record UUIDs plus the supplied/derived metric-field presence mask and a versioned canonical measurement digest (measurement_revision: 64 lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 characters; digest_schema_version: positive integer). Compute coverage from the incoming payload before merging with stored values: it must never inherit backfill-only fields. No raw transcript content enters coverage evidence. A duplicate-only import proves only the submitted UUIDs/fields/revisions. U-08 verifies that coverage masks/digests match all current metric inputs and selected usage representatives; later enrichment or snapshot selection not witnessed by a plugin leaves those inputs uncovered. Unknown identity/surface, incomplete coverage or conflicts cannot yield verified_capture. F18 tests partial late-turn receipt=false, full same-data hook coverage=true, and missing-usage receipt followed by native usage enrichment=false. M-18 session health can still count a valid partial receipt without claiming full verification.
rules.M-01: Windows apply to events, not sessions. A session contributes only its records with timestamp inside the window.
rules.M-02: Human message. role=user record that is not a tool-result carrier, not isMeta, not isSidechain, whose text is non-empty and does not start with <command-name>, <local-command-stdout>, [Request interrupted, or <system-reminder>. An input that a stored structural confirmation proves another agent submitted, or a task notification whose own line Claude Code marks as one (origin kind task-notification), is a confirmed automated input: it is neutral, never a human message, and contributes no characters, while the record stays stored and session, record and tool counts are unchanged. Only a structural proof confirms an input; producer labels, wording and timing do not. An input without one keeps this classification, which does not prove that a person submitted it. Human counts additionally exclude source-marked skill instructions, complete structured heartbeat inputs, and all user inputs in established agent-created conversations. These are separate sources or assumptions, not exact per-message sender confirmations. Valid question replies count answer text only; native image formatting is omitted while written requests, selected and pasted text remain. Unknown source does not prove a personal sender. The existing structural classification still defines agent-side turn and hands-off boundaries.
rules.M-03: Assistant turn. A maximal run of non-human records between two human messages. Assistant records are not turns. A confirmed automated input (M-02) is skipped: it neither bounds a run nor answers a human message, so it cannot form a turn by itself and does not split one.
rules.M-04: Tokens and cost, per host, surface and model. Count one usage row per API response. First dedupe storage by uuid (C-02); for Claude usage only, group rows with non-empty (message.id, requestId) and keep the latest timestamped snapshot, breaking equal timestamps deterministically by uuid. Missing either key falls back to that row's uuid, never a shared NULL group. Keep all content-block/tool rows for M-03/M-17. Deduplicate the response before applying M-01 to its selected usage timestamp, so a response crossing midnight or a window boundary cannot count twice. Include sidechains under their parent session; exclude <synthetic> and judge sessions. Sum the four canonical counters only when all four are measured; missing counters are not implicit zero. An incomplete selected usage observation makes that session's total unmeasured, while independently measured output may still be shown. Unknown model still contributes measured tokens. Cost uses the model price, 5m/1h cache-write split and service_tier. Codex canonical output_tokens is the reader's output delta and already contains reasoning output: any reasoning detail is informational and must not be added or priced a second time. Cache reads are already separated from fresh input by the reader. Cursor hook usage is attached once per generation and can enrich an existing UUID. Unknown model/missing tier price → cost — with the missing price named, tokens still counted. Costs use this same deduped usage projection and refresh on new/enriched usage and price-version changes. Store the price version; label every cost API-equivalent. Optional plan price is per host.
rules.M-05: Active spans. Per session, split the sorted event timeline wherever the gap exceeds 20 min; agent minutes = Σ span durations (parallel sessions add, by design).
rules.M-06: Concurrency. Sweep-line over all sessions' active spans: max = peak overlap; mean = Σ(k × minutes at overlap k) ÷ active wall minutes.
rules.M-07: Estimated Human minutes are counted input characters divided by the configured typing speed (five characters per word, default 40 WPM). Add every eligible message length, including selected or pasted text. A confirmed automated input (M-02), including a Claude Code task notification, a source-marked attachment, a complete heartbeat envelope, or an input in an established agent-created conversation contributes no Human time. Retained inputs are not independently proven personal submissions; a later person takeover of an agent-created conversation is also excluded. Use exact message timestamps for window and local-day membership. No response gaps, cap or overlap union. Missing eligible length or classification leaves the estimate unknown. This estimates input effort, not observed attention.
rules.M-08: Leverage = agent hours (M-05) ÷ your hours. Your hours are the times you sent messages to agents (the messages M-02 counts as yours), across all conversations and tools, on one timeline: two consecutive messages at most the break length apart count the whole gap between them; a longer gap is a break. The break length defaults to 60 min and is set in Settings. Stretches are split at local midnight; a message with no other within the break length adds no time. Agent hours and your hours both cover the same whole local days, from midnight of the selected range's first local day through the end of today; the previous period is the same number of whole local days just before. A day's leverage is that day's agent hours ÷ its own hours of yours. A stretch that began before a period's first midnight counts only from that midnight. An unknown sender classification leaves your hours unknown; zero or unknown your hours leave leverage unknown, never infinite.
rules.M-09: Hands-off stretch. From a human message to the last non-human agent event, including tool-result carriers, before the next human message, requiring ≥1 tool call; drop zero duration. A confirmed automated input (M-02) neither starts nor ends a stretch and is never its endpoint or tool evidence; agent events after it continue the current stretch, and a session whose only inputs are confirmed has none. It still counts as a user record for timestamp health. Evaluate timestamp health per surface: among sessions with ≥5 user/assistant records, a session is degenerate when distinct timestamps ×3 ≤ record count. Exclude a surface only when it has ≥3 qualifying sessions and >30% are degenerate; name it in coverage. Report median and p90 (sorted index floor(0.9×n), capped at n−1).
rules.M-10: Favorite model = model with the most output tokens in the selected window; the share card uses the ISO week. Only observations with measured output participate; input-only usage cannot invent a favorite model. Tie → most turns, attributing a turn to its first assistant record's model; any remaining tie is lexical model name for stable output.
rules.M-11: Linked-session tokens per merged PR = Σ M-04 over distinct sessions linked to that PR, within the selected event window; select PRs merged in the same window and report median per week. Values overlap when sessions link to several PRs; they are not exclusive PR costs. Gate token medians on ≥90% token+model coverage over a fixed trailing 14 days, excluding structurally unmeasured surfaces such as Cursor Agent CLI from the denominator while still naming them in coverage. Empty eligible denominator → —.
rules.M-11a: Linked-session agent hours per merged PR = Σ M-05 over the PR's distinct linked sessions in the same window; overlaps other PRs under the same rule as M-11.
rules.M-12: Linked-session human messages per merged PR = Σ M-02 over the PR's distinct linked sessions in the same window; median. Not gated by token coverage.
rules.M-12a: Linked-session hands-off per merged PR = median of M-09 stretches from those distinct sessions in the same window; does not add medians across sessions.
rules.M-13: Link ladder: exact (PR URL paired to a direct gh pr create tool result, validated hook provenance.github_pr_urls, or native Claude pr-link witness) > sha (gh api repos/{r}/commits/{sha}/pulls) > inferred (repo + branch). Scan content in memory and retain only canonical PR/structural witness fields in metadata mode; tool/result pairing survives batch boundaries. Inferred links are shown/badged and removed before aggregation when confirmed_only is on.
rules.M-14: Merged state and sizes from gh pr view --json state,mergedAt,additions,deletions,headRefName; derive merged from state == "MERGED" (mergedAt is the merge timestamp). merged is not a supported gh JSON field. Refresh hourly and on focus; failures retain previous values and mark them stale. A real-command shape check accompanies fixture responses.
rules.M-15: Estimated input effort = effective counted Human characters divided by the saved typing speed (five characters per word; default 40 WPM / 200 cpm). Includes selected or pasted text. Uses the same eligibility and character total as Human hours; always labelled "est.".
rules.M-16: Sessions per day counted by first in-window event; max/day and mean/day reported.
rules.M-17: Environment usage. Ingest derives structural name/kind (builtin, MCP server/tool, skill, hook, slash command, subagent) before content discard; metrics read those columns, never text_head or stored tool input. Slash commands come from command-name records; hook count means stop_hook_summary records, not individual hook invocations. Calls per day are grouped by host/surface; installed inventory comes from host registries, with unsupported inventory marked unknown. The panel lists installed-but-never-called items.
rules.M-18: Surface capture coverage. Per (host, raw source_surface), denominator = distinct discovered native sessions whose native start time is in the window; numerator = that same set with a successful plugin import receipt. Label this session-level health measure "sessions with a capture"; it is not complete measurement verification (U-08). Retain native start separately from M-16 first in-window event. Backfill/enrichment is not a plugin receipt. Receipts also retain exact submitted record/measurement coverage under C-08 so complete, partial and unknown coverage are distinguishable; last capture time is separate. Missing Python, unknown surface/start or inaccessible stores gives incomplete/unknown coverage. Refresh discovery at launch, focus/Detect again and every 60 s; F20 checks independent/new surfaces and F18 checks partial-vs-complete measurement coverage.
rules.M-19: PR aggregate totals and work type. A PR row keeps overlapping whole-linked-session effort (M-11/M-12). Any additive total across selected PRs first unions their distinct session IDs, then sums each session's in-window usage/messages/spans once. Type classification for that disjoint session set considers all eligible linked PR types: one distinct type → that type; multiple types → mixed; no eligible links → other. confirmed_only first removes inferred links. Daily token series uses event day, not merge day; PR counts dedupe PR IDs independently. With one 100k-token session linked to two exact PRs of different types, both PR rows show 100k with the overlap label, the distinct-session total is 100k, and the type series contributes 100k to mixed.
rules.O-11: Detection is per SURFACE, not per host. Each host ships several surfaces (CLI, desktop app, IDE extension, headless exec) and they do not share hook wiring, so a per-host check reports "connected" while a surface is silently dead. Surfaces are discovered, never enumerated in code
rules.O-12: Capture coverage per surface is the health signal. For each surface seen in the window: sessions started, sessions captured, and the ratio. A surface with sessions and zero captures renders "not capturing" with its own reason, never a host-level "connected".
rules.P-01: Metadata-only storage. Derive hygiene flags, text lengths, usage, and tool classifications in memory, then discard free text before persistence. New/updated rows must not acquire content_json, raw_json, text_head, transcript-derived titles, tool input/output, excerpts or content-bearing evidence. Existing saved content remains unchanged; duplicate enrichment cannot add new content while this mode is active. Counts, structural names, IDs and source provenance remain available. Test fresh imports and enriched duplicate UUIDs, including tool and fire rows. One exception keeps a little text in this mode: a one-line preview of at most 280 characters of each input the stored classification calls a person's whole message, and of each proven Claude Code task notification's own summary, so the Dashboard can show them without reopening source files. Readers still choose the message by its current classification; explicit purge clears these previews too.
rules.P-02: Explicit content purge. Only the separate confirmed deletion action clears previously stored transcript content/raw JSON/text_head, prompt-derived titles, tool input/output, excerpts and content-bearing evidence or judge results from the app database. Preserve counts, usage, structural identities and provenance; invalidate content-dependent views. Enforce P-01 afterward so retries cannot refill purged content while metadata-only is enabled. Original host files are never modified by this action.
rules.R-05: Fires store fire_id, logical rule_id/rule_version, origin_sink/rule_source_id, optional resolved rule_instance_id, timestamps/native session identity, structural rule/tool/decision/outcome fields and local judged result. Unknown external rule metadata may hydrate read-only but cannot activate executable content. C-04 governs retries and P-01/P-02 content persistence. Adherence trend = fires per 100 opportunities/week; FP rate = judged fp ÷ all judged.
rules.R-08: Judge overhead tokens spent by judge calls are counted separately and shown on the Rulebook screen, never mixed into session tokens.
rules.U-03: A tile whose input is entirely unmeasured (F7, Cursor CLI only) renders — and the coverage line names the reason.
rules.U-08: The card renders from the same signed aggregate as submission; the aggregate never includes repo names, paths, content or private record-coverage evidence. verified_capture is true only when plugin receipts cover every transcript-derived metric-contributing record and every M-04 selected usage representative at the exact measurement revision used by that aggregate. A receipt for one late turn cannot verify older backfill-only records/usage. F18 tests partial late-turn coverage=false, complete same-data hook coverage=true, and later unobserved usage enrichment=false again. This badge describes capture provenance, not independent attestation of an open-source client.
